# The Weight of Glass

The sea had a way of speaking to Eamon in languages he no longer understood. Twelve years on the island of Carrant, and he'd learned its moods the way a man learns a dead wife's breathing—by absence, by the particular silence where sound should be.

He found the bottle on a Tuesday, which was the kind of day the sea chose to be cruel. The waves had come in high and black, chewing at the granite base of the lighthouse with a patience that made his teeth ache. When the storm broke at dawn, the shore was littered with wreckage: kelp, splintered driftwood, the bleached ribs of some forgotten vessel. And there, tucked beneath a tangle of rope, a green glass bottle, no larger than his fist, its cork swollen and dark.
